summary: Wave 4 ad-hoc review (not bound to a mission-e39d21fa requirement/criterion -- separate review request). env.schema.ts staging gate widening and both queue-processor tenant-context wrappings (ai-jobs.processor.ts, external-data.processor.ts) check out: apps/api/.env.staging already sets RBAC_PERSISTED_AUTHORITY=ON so the gate has a real path to pass, and both processors route every DB-writing job-name branch through DatabaseContextService.runInTenantContext consistent with the pre-existing ALS-proxy pattern used by notifications.processor.ts. However the users.service.ts privilege-escalation fix is incomplete: assertCanAssignRole() now correctly checks is_assignable (verified against the roles seed migration where super_admin.is_assignable=FALSE, exercised by the new assert-can-assign-role.security.spec.ts), but UsersService.create() -- reachable via POST /users gated only by @RequireRole('owner') -- sets org_members.role directly from CreateUserDto.role (a free-form slug-regex-validated string) via MembershipRoleResolverService.resolveOrThrow(), which never checks is_assignable or hierarchy_level. A tenant owner can still grant a brand-new member the global super_admin role by calling POST /users instead of PATCH /users/:id/role, reproducing the exact privilege-escalation class the fix claims to close via an unpatched, untested sibling code path. See finding find-f7bfdd94.
